documents.title: PHX-142 — Auth redirect loop after SSO cutover
documents.content:
Key: PHX-142
Summary: Auth redirect loop after SSO cutover
Type: Bug
Status: Blocked
Priority: Highest
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Daniel Okonkwo
Reporter: Priya Raghunathan
Due date: 2026-11-10
Created: 2026-11-02
Updated: 2026-11-16
Labels: auth, sso, sev1
Components: Billing Platform / Auth

Description

Since the SSO cutover on 2026-11-01, customers who sign in through the Northwind Okta tenant land on the billing settings page, get bounced to the identity provider, and come back to the same page. The loop never terminates and no session cookie is issued, so the billing settings page is unreachable for roughly 12% of daily active users.

Support has logged 412 tickets in eleven days. Clearing cookies and retrying in a private window works about half the time. Refunds and payment-method changes are the worst affected flows because both require re-authentication.

Root-cause hypothesis: the identity provider metadata imported on 2026-10-28 still advertises the legacy assertion consumer service URL for the billing application. Okta treats the callback as a new sign-in instead of a continuation of the existing session. Daniel reproduced this locally with a stale service-provider metadata file and has a one-line configuration fix ready.

Ruled out: the CDN cache rules, the session cookie domain change, and the Ledger v2 rollout. All three were bisected out of the 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-02 deploy range.
documents.author: Priya Raghunathan

documents.title: PHX-131 — Alice Migration: import legacy customer records into Ledger v2
documents.content:
Key: PHX-131
Summary: Alice Migration: import legacy customer records into Ledger v2
Type: Epic
Status: In Progress
Priority: High
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Mei-Ling Zhou
Reporter: Priya Raghunathan
Due date: 2026-11-14
Created: 2026-10-06
Updated: 2026-11-15
Labels: migration, ledger-v2, alice
Components: Billing Platform / Data

Description

Alice Migration is the internal codename for the account-record import from the legacy ledger into Ledger v2. It is not named after a person and it is not a team, despite what the name suggests.

Scope: 9.8 million customer account records, 41 million balance snapshots, and 2.3 million stored payment-method references. The import runs in batches of 50,000 rows with a checkpoint written after every batch, so a failed run resumes instead of restarting.

Progress at the 2026-11-13 checkpoint: 4.2 million account records and 1.1 million balance snapshots migrated. Sustained throughput is 180,000 rows per hour, which puts the account-record pass about six days behind the original estimate of 2026-11-14.

Constraints agreed with the billing team:
- Customer email addresses and phone numbers are copied verbatim by design. Redaction happens at retrieval time, never at rest.
- No account id may be re-keyed. Downstream finance exports join on the legacy id.
- The legacy ledger stays writable until 2026-12-01 so the import can be rolled back.

Open question: whether the 2.3 million payment-method references need re-tokenization before cutover, or can be copied as opaque blobs and re-tokenized afterwards. Ines Vega owns that decision.
documents.author: Priya Raghunathan

documents.title: PHX-150 — Cut over billing webhooks to Ledger v2
documents.content:
Key: PHX-150
Summary: Cut over billing webhooks to Ledger v2
Type: Story
Status: In Progress
Priority: High
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Daniel Okonkwo
Reporter: Priya Raghunathan
Due date: 2026-11-20
Created: 2026-10-20
Updated: 2026-11-16
Labels: billing, webhooks, cutover
Components: Billing Platform / Webhooks

Description

Move inbound payment-provider webhooks from the legacy ledger endpoint to the Ledger v2 consumer. The new consumer validates signatures, writes to an append-only event table, and is replay-safe.

Plan:
1. Dual-write both consumers for five business days and compare payload counts hourly.
2. Flip the primary endpoint behind the phoenix.webhooks.primary flag.
3. Keep the legacy consumer deployed but idle for ten days as a rollback path.

Acceptance criteria:
- No duplicate billing events for the same provider event id.
- Event lag stays under 30 seconds at p95.
- Reconciliation totals from PHX-147 match on three consecutive days.

The idempotency work in PHX-155 is a hard dependency: without it, a provider retry during the dual-write window double-posts to Ledger v2. The Nimbus schema v3 upgrade (PHX-152) is a soft dependency, but shipping the cutover before the vendor schema stabilises means doing the comparison twice.
documents.author: Priya Raghunathan

documents.title: PHX-147 — Reconcile November invoices against the legacy ledger
documents.content:
Key: PHX-147
Summary: Reconcile November invoices against the legacy ledger
Type: Task
Status: In Review
Priority: High
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Ravi Chandrasekaran
Reporter: Priya Raghunathan
Due date: 2026-11-23
Created: 2026-11-03
Updated: 2026-11-15
Labels: billing, reconciliation, finance
Components: Billing Platform / Finance

Description

Compare every November invoice in Ledger v2 against the legacy ledger and explain every difference above one cent. Finance will not sign off on the cutover without this.

Method: nightly extract of both ledgers into the finance mart, joined on account id and invoice period. Differences are bucketed into rounding, proration, double-posted refunds, and missing events.

Current state: 1,284 of 320,000 invoices differ. 1,271 are rounding differences under one cent caused by the legacy ledger's float arithmetic. Nine are prorations for mid-cycle plan changes, which are expected. Four are genuine double-posted refunds, all in the EU region, all traced to the incident in PHX-138.

Deliverable: a reconciliation note posted to the Phoenix status page by 2026-11-23, with the four double-posted refunds either corrected or explicitly accepted by Finance.

documents.title: PHX-155 — Add idempotency keys to the payment capture API
documents.content:
Key: PHX-155
Summary: Add idempotency keys to the payment capture API
Type: Story
Status: To Do
Priority: High
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Ines Vega
Reporter: Daniel Okonkwo
Due date: 2026-11-20
Created: 2026-11-04
Updated: 2026-11-14
Labels: payments, reliability, idempotency
Components: Billing Platform / Payments

Description

The capture endpoint currently creates a new charge for every request, so a client retry after a timeout double-charges the customer. Add an Idempotency-Key header, persist the key with the charge result, and return the stored response for a replay within 24 hours.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replaying an identical request returns the original charge id and HTTP 200, never a second charge.
- Reusing a key with a different request body returns HTTP 409.
- Keys expire after 24 hours and the expiry sweep runs hourly.
- The charge table gains a unique index on (merchant_id, idempotency_key).

This blocks PHX-150: the webhook cutover dual-write window would double-post without idempotent capture.

documents.title: PHX-160 — Load test Ledger v2 at 3x peak traffic
documents.content:
Key: PHX-160
Summary: Load test Ledger v2 at 3x peak traffic
Type: Task
Status: To Do
Priority: Medium
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Mei-Ling Zhou
Reporter: Priya Raghunathan
Due date: 2026-12-04
Created: 2026-11-06
Updated: 2026-11-12
Labels: performance, ledger-v2
Components: Billing Platform / Platform

Description

Run a sustained load test against the Ledger v2 read and write paths at three times the November peak: 4,200 writes per second and 11,000 reads per second for two hours.

Success criteria: p99 write latency under 120 milliseconds, no connection pool exhaustion, no replication lag above two seconds, and a clean 30-minute soak at peak afterwards.

Use the production-shaped dataset restored from the 2026-11-10 snapshot, not synthetic rows: the previous run was invalidated because the synthetic data had no hot accounts and hid the row-lock contention on account_balance.

Result should be posted as a comment on this issue with the Grafana snapshot links. Do not run the test during the Phoenix cutover window.

Once Ledger v2 serves all reads, the three legacy read replicas cost roughly 1,900 dollars a month and serve nothing. Retire them two weeks after cutover, not before: the rollback path in PHX-150 depends on the legacy primary remaining available, and the replicas are what makes a read-only rollback possible.

Steps: confirm zero connections for seven consecutive days, revoke the replica credentials, snapshot the volumes for the audit archive, then delete the instances. Announce in #billing-platform before the snapshot.

documents.title: PHX-138 — Customer refunds double-posted in the EU region
documents.content:
Key: PHX-138
Summary: Customer refunds double-posted in the EU region
Type: Bug
Status: Done
Priority: Highest
Project: Project Phoenix (PHX)
Assignee: Daniel Okonkwo
Reporter: Priya Raghunathan
Due date: 2026-11-06
Created: 2026-10-29
Updated: 2026-11-07
Labels: incident, refunds, eu
Components: Billing Platform / Payments

Description

Between 2026-10-29 02:00 and 06:00 UTC, 214 refunds in the EU region were posted twice. The refund worker retried on a read timeout after the primary had already committed, and the retry had no idempotency key.

Customer impact: 214 customers received a double refund totalling 18,412 euros. Finance clawed back the duplicates from 197 accounts; 17 accounts had already withdrawn the funds and were written off.

Fix applied on 2026-10-30: the refund worker now writes a dedupe row keyed on the provider refund id before calling the ledger, and treats a duplicate-key conflict as success. The deeper fix is PHX-155, which generalises the same idea to capture.

Postmortem action items: add a refund-specific alert on duplicate provider ids, and include refund replays in the monthly reconciliation sample.
documents.author: Priya Raghunathan

Due date: 2026-11-27
Created: 2026-11-05
Updated: 2026-11-11
Labels: vendor, webhooks, nimbus
Components: Billing Platform / Webhooks

Description

Nimbus Systems, our payment provider, is moving webhook payloads from schema v2 to v3. The v3 payload renames the event id field, adds a mandatory signature version, and splits the refund object out of the charge object.

Blocked: the draft v3 documentation differs from the sandbox payloads we captured on 2026-11-10, and the vendor has not confirmed which is authoritative. Until the vendor ships the final spec (now promised for 2026-11-24), any parser we write is guesswork.

Impact if it slips past 2026-11-27: the PHX-150 cutover comparison runs against a moving target and we either redo the dual-write window or accept an untested parser in production.

Description

The account-record import in PHX-131 copies the current balance but not the daily balance history, so the Ledger v2 dashboard shows a flat line for the 4.2 million migrated accounts. Backfill the last 90 days of snapshots from the legacy balance_snapshot table.

The backfill is 3.7 billion rows, so it runs as a partitioned job: one partition per month, smallest first, throttled at 20,000 rows per second so it cannot drown the cutover traffic.

Constraint: snapshots must be written with the original observation timestamp, not the backfill time, or the dashboard's range queries will be wrong. Ravi has a dry run on 2026-11-12 that reproduced the first month correctly.

documents.title: Root cause is stale IdP metadata
documents.content:
Confirmed the root cause this morning. The service-provider metadata file that our Okta integration imported on 2026-10-28 still lists the legacy assertion consumer service URL for the billing app. Okta keeps treating the callback as a brand new sign-in request, which is exactly the loop we see.

The fix is to re-import the metadata with the current ACS URL. It is a one-line change in the integration config, not a code deploy. I need an Okta administrator to apply it because the integration is managed outside our Terraform workspace.

Priya, can you get me the Okta admin on this today? I have pinged the identity team but the ticket is sitting in their queue. If we cannot get it applied before 2026-11-18, we should ship the cookie-scope workaround as an interim measure.
documents.author: Daniel Okonkwo

documents.title: Escalating to the weekly incident review
documents.content:
This is now the top support driver: 412 tickets and a 12% failure rate on sign-in for paying customers. I am escalating it to the weekly incident review on 2026-11-18 unless the Okta change lands first.

Daniel, I need a written confirmation by 2026-11-18 that either the metadata is fixed or the interim cookie-scope workaround is live. If both slip, the billing settings page stays effectively down for one in eight customers, and Finance cannot take payment-method changes.

Reach me on my mobile if the admin access comes through outside working hours: +1-415-555-0142. Support is tracking this as SEV-1 and the billing-ops alias is on every update.
documents.author: Priya Raghunathan

documents.title: Slipping the cutover to 2026-11-27
documents.content:
We are moving the webhook cutover to 2026-11-27. Two reasons: Nimbus has not shipped the schema v3 spec (PHX-152 is blocked on them), and the idempotency work in PHX-155 has not started, so a provider retry during the dual-write window would double-post.

I would rather run the dual-write against the final v3 payload once than run it twice against a patchwork. The rollback path is unchanged, and the legacy consumer stays primary until the flag flips.

New target: dual-write starts 2026-11-27, primary flag flips 2026-12-04.
documents.author: Daniel Okonkwo

documents.title: The Jira due date still says 2026-11-20
documents.content:
Noting the mismatch for the record: the due date field on this issue still says 2026-11-20, but the comment above says the cutover moved to 2026-11-27. Please update the field, because the weekly status report and the finance timeline both read the field, not the comments.

Until the field changes I am reporting PHX-150 as due this week. If the date is moving, updating the issue is the one action that keeps every downstream report honest.

documents.title: Migration checkpoint: 4.2M of 9.8M
documents.content:
Checkpoint from the overnight run: 4.2 million of 9.8 million account records migrated, 1.1 million balance snapshots. Throughput held at 180,000 rows per hour, so the account-record pass lands around 2026-11-20 rather than the 2026-11-14 on the issue.

Two clarifications for anyone reading the tracker cold: Alice Migration is our codename for this import, not a person and not a team, so please do not add it to the people directory. And the customer email addresses in the migrated rows are intentionally left as-is; the PII scrubber runs when chunks are retrieved for an answer, never at rest.

Next checkpoint Thursday. No blockers on my side; the payment-method re-tokenization decision from Ines is the only open dependency.

He also said the refund-object split will be behind a per-tenant flag for the first month, which means our parser has to handle both shapes during the transition. I have asked for the flag schedule in writing.

documents.title: Reconciliation deltas: four real double-posts
documents.content:
Reconciliation is done except for the four genuine deltas. Breakdown of the 1,284 differences: 1,271 rounding under one cent, nine prorations for mid-cycle upgrades, four double-posted EU refunds from the PHX-138 incident.

The four are accounts 88421, 90577, 91830, and 93412, all refunded twice on 2026-10-29. I have the correction journal ready; Finance needs to approve it before I can close this issue.

Ines reviewed the correction entries with me on 2026-11-14 and agrees they are right. She is not the owner of this issue, just the reviewer.
